title: nav-pilot agentpakke manifest (v1)
description: Contract between an agentpakke repo and the nav-pilot binary. Lives at .nav-pilot/agentpakke.json in the agentpakke repo. Unknown client keys, context keys, and additional fields are ignored by consumers (A3/A4), so growth of the ecosystem never invalidates an existing manifest on an older binary. Parenthesised ids such as (A1) and (G3) are decision ids defined in the PRD at https://github.com/navikt/copilot/issues/435.

mcpServerName.description: Name of a server in Nav's MCP registry (https://mcp-registry.nav.no), in the registry's own reverse-DNS form: <namespace>/<name>, as in io.github.navikt/github-mcp. The pattern is the registry's own name format and constrains the shape only. Membership is checked against the live registry when nav-pilot validates or installs, because the registry moves independently of nav-pilot releases: a list frozen into the schema would reject a server added after this version shipped.

relativePath.description: Repo-relative path. Absolute paths and parent traversal are rejected by nav-pilot's semantic validation.

privateDomain.description: One DNS name whose lookup resolves to a private address, named in full and one at a time. No scheme, no port, no path, no wildcard.

cpltProposalReason.description: Why this agentpakke needs the waiver, in one or two sentences. Shown verbatim in the consent prompt, so it is the only thing the person deciding has to go on.

cpltProposal.description: Sandbox configuration proposed in cplt's own vocabulary. v1 defines exactly one proposable setting, proxy.allow_private_domains: a DNS-rebinding waiver naming hosts one at a time. It is not a permission — the allowlist and the blocklist still apply, no port is opened, no path is granted, nothing is executed. Everything a repo must never propose (preset, allow.exec, repo_dirs, inherit_env, allowed_domains, blocked_domains, proxy.forced, the guards) is refused here rather than ignored. Other keys are tolerated for forward compatibility, but nav-pilot reports them as inert and never honours them.

contractVersion.description: Manifest schema-and-semantics version. nav-pilot supports major version 1.

name.description: Agentpakke identity. Recorded as the install's collection name (the agentpakke manifest supersedes the collection manifest).

owner.description: Attribution only; the install source is wherever the manifest was cloned from.

clients.description: One entry per supported client (keys today: copilot, opencode, pi). Keys are pattern-validated, not enumerated: a consumer MUST ignore client keys it does not recognize — that client is unavailable, the manifest stays valid (A3/A4). Tier is derived from shape: an entry with `payloads` is Tier 2; an entry relying on the top-level `layout` is Tier 1 (A1).

primaryAgents.description: Agent names treated as primary personas for this client (C1-C2). Every other agent materializes as a subagent. Optional: a Tier 1 entry that ships no agent omits it, and nav-pilot then refuses to launch that client because there is no persona to hand it, while install and sync carry the pakke's other content as usual. Declaring it commits the pakke to a layout.agents directory holding a file per name. Ignored for a Tier 2 entry, where the roster belongs to each payload tree: see clients.<client>.payloads.<context>.primaryAgents.

compatibility.description: Supported client version RANGE (A1); exact pins belong only to the local/security-profile tier (M4).

defaultModel.description: Default model id, or the literal "inherit" (F3).

defaultContext.description: Which payload context launches by default (G3); defaults to "full".

payloads.description: Tier 2: one entry per context (keys today: full, focused) — same ignore-unknown rule as client keys. Each payload declares its own primaryAgents, because the payload tree is what carries the agents. Payload manifest is `<path>/manifest.json` by convention (A7); `manifest` only overrides that.

primaryAgents.description: Agent names launchable in this context. The first element is the context's default persona. Required: a payload tree carries its own agents, so a context roster cannot be inferred from the client entry (C1-C2).

layout.description: Tier 1 clients only: repo-relative paths to content directories (D1). Declare the directories the pakke actually ships and no others: a skills-only or instructions-only pakke omits `agents`, and a pakke declaring primaryAgents must declare `agents`. At least one of the known directories must be named — unknown keys stay valid (A3/A4) but nav-pilot reads none of them, so a layout made only of those would materialize nothing.

provenance.description: For composed content (H2): base repo + digest, overlay components with versions.

policies.description: Optional pointers to policy artifacts materialized by nav-pilot for Tier 1 clients (E1), plus the sandbox configuration this agentpakke proposes to whoever installs it (propose).

propose.description: Sandbox configuration this agentpakke asks the installing user to consent to, keyed by the tool it is expressed in and written in that tool's own vocabulary. A proposal configures nothing by itself: it becomes launch flags only after an interactive approval, and only for the scope that approved it. Tool keys this nav-pilot does not implement are ignored (A3/A4), so pi and opencode can be defined later without invalidating an existing manifest.

profiles.description: Optional launch profiles: a directory of profile files plus the manifest-declared default (E2).

mcpServers.description: MCP servers this agentpakke's agents and skills expect, named as they are in Nav's MCP registry. Every name must be one the registry publishes; nav-pilot asks the registry at validate and install time, and a name it does not publish is a violation. Declaring one does not configure it: nav-pilot writes no MCP configuration for any client, and enabling a server stays the user's action. install names what the pakke needs and points at the registry.

minNavPilotVersion.description: Minimum nav-pilot version required, in the release format YYYY.MM.DD-HHMMSS-sha7 (the build sha is optional). A value outside this format is rejected rather than ignored: nav-pilot cannot compare it, so accepting it would silently disable the gate the manifest asked for.
